utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please be seated, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. The affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. When we finished yesterday, we were talking about the forms, specifically we were talking about the authors of crimes and the options that were there. Did you have an opportunity to refresh your memory about what options would have been there?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We appear, Ms. O'Leary, not to be getting any translation at the moment. The interpretation is faltering. Are you able now to receive any interpretation, Mr. Haxhibeqiri?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we try again. Is there any interpretation reaching you yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll just have to wait, I am afraid, there seems to be a connection problem. We just must wait a moment, a technician is checking. I will try once again to ask you whether you are now receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I heard the witness answer, but no interpretation has reached us. There must still be a connection problem. I will try once again now. Are you able to tell me whether you receive any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It appears it may now be functioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What you are saying is apparently reaching the interpreter's booth, but the connection back from that booth is not functioning. So with a little more patience.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness might be on the English channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is the witness on the English channel? Perhaps if the interpreters could please speak to me from the Albanian booth. Nothing is coming through. So we still have no connection from the Albanian booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are advised that there is a technical problem. It may take up to ten minutes to fix it. We will therefore adjourn. This is just to keep you on your mettle, Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the Albanian booth please speak so we could test it once, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn for 10 minutes. --- Break taken at 2.31 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are informed that the technical problem has now been overcome. Are you hearing me, Mr. Haxhibeqiri?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We are receiving a translation from your answer. Ms. O'Leary, if you would please continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, would you like me to repeat the question that I asked or did you hear it before we went on the technical break?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. I will start to read. "Are you prepared to testify in front of The Hague Tribunal?" That was the first question.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And can I just interrupt you. You are reading from one of the sample forms that you had done with the --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the interview form, the questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Is this interview form filled in that you are reading from right now?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But it's representative of the same form that was used for everyone; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, a primary concern, if we could just focus on -- in your last testimony you had said, Please describe the authors of the crime, is what the form says. For example the VJ, the police, the paramilitary, or civilians. Is that what it says when asked to list the author of the crime?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read that out. Sorry. "Were you a victim or a witness to the crime, such as murders, tortures, sexual abuse, kidnapping, destruction of property, looting, persecution, displacement? Please describe on the blank page. If you need more space, you may use an additional blank page." There are five pages here where one could explain what had happened to him or her. Later on, we continue with each individual crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. Very specifically though, I'm interested only in the one part of that form, what it says about who the possible perpetrators were, what options were listed. If you could read that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Please describe the perpetrators of the crime; the VJ, the police, paramilitary, civilians."

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And that's all the options that are listed there; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is more: "How were they dressed, what uniform, what weapons, what vehicles and other equipment were they using."

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. It does not list on there, though, the KLA or NATO as a possible alleged perpetrator of a crime, does it?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was from NATO, then the witness has specifically said it was because of the NATO bombing. It was the witness that specified that in the description of what had happened to them. When they described what had happened to them, they specified these details.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so in the narrative did they also describe if it was KLA as perpetrators of crime?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But they would have to specify that in their own language, just in their own narrative, not specifically a check box; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move on to your statement now.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we could have P1068 put on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And I want to focus first on the statistics you have.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Specifically if we are focusing in on about the fourth page in the English. It's also -- it's on page 2 right away which is page 5 in e-court in English, which would be page 2 of the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: First of all, you said that the last true census was carried out in 1981. What do you mean by true census?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that was the only and the last census and the statistics that are being quoted today are from that census.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I am afraid we are having a little technical difficulty, but I'll just ask you some questions without putting the statement at this moment while we get that on the screen. What censuses were available -- has any census been done since 1981 in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So there was a census done in 1991?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the Albanians were not included in that census.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why were the Albanians not included in that census?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a demographer, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But it seems from some of the other numbers that you've given that the Albanians were obviously a majority of the population, especially in the municipality of Gjakova. Do you know of any reason why you say that, that they were not included?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why? A state which uses repressive measures and tanks against our -- our parliament and closes down the university and other schools, that state loses the confidence of the population, and that happened soon after the autonomy of Kosova was revoked.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So did the Albanian population boycott that census then?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But I know that they did not take part. They were not included in that census.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You were there at the time, correct, in Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why did you not take part in the census then?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody invited me.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How do you know a census was taken then?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Let's move on to some of the statistics that we have here also in your statement. You estimate - because you said that an accurate census was not done in 1991 in your statement here you say - you estimate that the population of the town - and we're on page 2 here, about a third of the way down: "In 1998, 1999 I would estimate that the population of the town was about 120.000 total." And that would have been the population of Gjakova city; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's according the last census.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you felt that the population had not fluctuated very much between the 1981 census and then in 1998?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it has changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you are saying that actually in 1998 there would have been more or less people in Gjakova city than 120.000?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could have been more, could have been more, about 150.000 or so.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And how many people do you estimate were in Gjakova municipality, as a total?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about 1988?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: 150.000 for the city of Gjakova, correct, and how many for the entire municipality, if you would guess?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about the municipality here. And here in the statement it's just the population of the town, of the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's a mistake here. On the third paragraph, the population of the town was 120.000, but that included the municipality, so the town and the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So it's your testimony today that it was approximately 120-, to 150.000 in the entire municipality of Gjakova in 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1981 there were 120.000 in total, whereas in 1998, 150.000 for the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Do you have any idea, any estimate, about how many people were living in Kosovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 2 million.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And I want to focus a little bit further down then, because you say that: "Since that time," since 1998 you are discussing, "500.000 to 700.000 Kosovo Albanians have been forced to leave the country as a result of persecution." So when you say "the country," are you referring to Kosovo or are you referring to a larger area?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So in the ten years of 1988 to 1998, you are saying roughly one-fourth to one half of the population of Kosovar Albanians left?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 500.000 is not half but is one-fourth. Mainly youth. These are figures that I have collected from the daily press.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Correct. My math skills are not the best but one-fourth I was saying as far as 500.000 but you give a range of 700.000, so I was saying one fourth to one half. When you say mainly youth left, were they possibly leaving for employment?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were forced to leave because of the violence. They obviously did not have anywhere to work, but they were also being persecuted, and they were being forced to join the army; but they did not trust that state and didn't want to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were Serbs or Romas, youths specifically, leaving at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't have problems then. They could do whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You state here that: "The number of non-Albanians in the town never exceeded 2 per cent." It's directly under that 120.000 number. If we're going with 120.000 or 150.000, wouldn't that be about 2-, 3.000 people that would have been non-Albanian?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I came to this Tribunal, I read a few figures from the statistical centre of Serbia related to Kosova. There I read that in 1991 the number of Serbs in the Gjakove municipality was 1.475 this is a statistical figure from Belgrade. So it was 1.475 or -57; I'm not sure about this. This is something that I can confirm. There were other ethnic groups like the Roma, Montenegrin, Croatians, Bosnians; but the overall figure is no more than 5 per cent. 5 per cent of other groups. They could go up to 5 per cent, but the majority, 95 per cent of the population, was Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so by these figures you've looked up, it was 1.475 or -57 Serbs in all of the municipality of Gjakova, in 1991.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Let's move on a little further down your statement where you are talking about education. On page 2, paragraph 3 from the bottom, at least in the English version, it starts off with: "Many of the people who left..." that paragraph. You state that the schools were closed to Albanians. What do you mean by closed?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The secondary schools for the Albanians starting from 1990, they were closed. Initially the police was in front of the school gates with tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: This is in 1990?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was starting from 1990 for the next ten years up until the NATO bombing started. That was the case for all the secondary schools, high schools in Kosova including the universities. And schooling for the Albanians took place in private homes for ten years. For the Serb kids, there was schools, there were schools. And as for the Albanian students, they continued with their education secretly, in private homes. And they were exposed to real dangers if they were found holding Albanian books and Albanian textbooks. Their books were torn and they were tortured.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Let me just cut you off quickly because we do have this in your statement almost verbatim what you're explaining now. And I just want to ask a you couple of questions to clarify a couple things I didn't understand about them. When you refer to the tanks - you don't refer to it in your statement - but you are saying now that there were tanks positioned outside the secondary schools for ten years?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What hasn't been written on this statement has been witnessed by myself in person. I've seen it with my own eyes. It's true that it hasn't been included in this statement, but the statement is not a complete one. There are so many things which have not been included in this one that I have witnessed myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But I believe you were given an opportunity in the last trial you testified at of Milutinovic et al. To explain anything else that you had eye-witnessed; the Judges gave you an opportunity to discuss anything else that was not in the statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You haven't read the transcript. I have said it very very clearly that the tanks were deployed in front of the schools. I am an eye-witness to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That's correct. You did say that. But at this point, you are saying -- it sounds like, that the tanks were there for all ten years. Is that true, or was it just 1990, 1991? How long were the tanks there?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that the tanks were positioned there throughout these ten years. I said in the beginning. And that sends a clear message, when you see police presence with tanks outside a school, that means that the school is closed down.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: It may just be language here, but when you say "closed down" do you mean that the entire school was closed to everyone then in 1990?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to Albanians, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But at some point the tanks were moved; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't remember when they were moved, but they didn't stay there for a long time. But that was enough to keep Albanians away from school buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it permissible then in 1998 for an Albanian child to enroll in the school?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that situation continued. As of 1990, the Albanian children were no longer able to continue their higher education.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And what about the elementary schools? Were there tanks in front of the elementary schools in 1990?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those schools were open.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did Albanian children continue to attend the elementary schools in Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And that's through 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when you're discussing the secondary schools and the university, you said that it was conducted in secret. Was it impermissible under the governing constitution at that time to set up these, I think it's referred to the parallel school system; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which governing constitution are you talking about, the one that used tanks?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm speaking of the governing constitution of the state in 1998.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which state are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm asking if the government permitted these parallel school systems to exist. Did they in any way forbid them or try to shut them down?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It permitted it.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why then did you say a little bit earlier that they were conducted in secret?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about secondary education and universities. They did permit the elementary education system, but not the high one.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you are saying that because some elementary children chose to go to the parallel school system instead of the existing schools; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Then let's talk about the secondary school system. Did the government in any way forbid these parallel secret school systems or in any way try to shut them down?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it tried to shut them down. I mentioned the tanks positioned outside school buildings, and that's why the Albanians organised themselves to study in private homes. And this is what they did for a long period of time, for ten years.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But the tanks were positioned outside schools that were attended by both Albanians, Serbs, and other minorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one secondary school was attended by Serb students.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What was the name of that school, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hydar Dushe [phoen] high school.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: In 1990 was there a tank outside the Hydar Dushe school?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But at that point the Albanian secondary students stopped going and started attending the parallel school system; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And the Hydar Dushe school remained open then with Serbs and other minorities?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What other minorities were in Gjakova that would have been attending a secondary school such as that?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosniaks, Romas.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And it would have been operating then with a dramatically less population of students then after 1990 if all Albanian students left; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I know is that every year just one class would attend school from the first to the fourth year of secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we could move on to the next topic you discuss in your statement, one more paragraph down, of health care. You briefly touch on it. It seems, though, that your main concern of that in Gjakova was that there were two Serbs in high-ranking positions at that time. I'm talking about the second line of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there was the hospital and the health centre. Just like in every other organisation and institution, the violent measures were in place; and that's why here the Albanian directors were removed from their jobs and replaced by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: This is two positions you are talking about, though, here; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Albanians were removed, and they were replaced by Serbs, Serb doctors.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you know when this was?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember, but it is during this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But there were other Albanian doctors and specialists working in the health care centre and hospital; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Would you say the majority of doctors were Albanian?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And Albanians and Serbs at that time, as far as I could understand here, were receiving adequate health care similarly throughout the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then you go on to discuss television and media that was in the area at that time. What Albanian media continued through 1998 and 1999, specifically, which television was available?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had one television, the KTV. In fact, that was the Prishtina radio television which was shut down in July 1990. The police brutally entered the premises and removed the employees from their offices. They also had tanks positioned there. And from that day, this television was closed down and it was opened only after the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And we do have some of this in your statement, it should be, I'm going pretty much straight through it, if you want, for reference, to see what was already contained in your statement. You said that you were receiving Serb propaganda at some point. "We got Serb propaganda all the time which was always anti-Albanian." This is on page 3 in the English at the very top. The Albanian may be page 3, page 4. When did this Serb propaganda start?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after Milosevic came into power. It started systematically and intensified in the years prior to the war. Three years before the war started, to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't want to cut you off, but when did those programs end then, or do they still continue?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the NATO bombing started, everything came to an end.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were you able to access satellite television at that time with Albanian programmes?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And going to the newspapers then, you say the Serbs gave permission for one newspaper; and I'm afraid I'll ruin the name but --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, when I said another TV channel in Albanian, I was referring to TVSH, the Albanian satellite television.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And that continued to function through 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole time, yes. That was the only source of information for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And there was no propaganda of any kind on that station?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What kind of propaganda do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, you classified what was on the other station as Serb propaganda. I'm asking if there was any kind of propaganda on this TVSH?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. They conveyed the news of Albanian media from Albania for 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it a station that supported independent Kosovo, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then moving on to the newspapers as we were just -- I was attempting to mention the name of this newspaper, "Bujku." The Serbs gave permission for one newspaper "Bujku." Do you know what group published that newspaper?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The owner of the MUP is Veton Surroi.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were there any other newspapers at that time that were functioning in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, "Rilindija" at the time was forced to change its name into "Bujku," whereas "Koha Ditore" is a newspaper owned by Veton Surroi.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. Was "Koha Ditore" - excuse me in my pronunciation - was that functioning in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's a detail and unfortunately I don't remember it. I think it did, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: The reason I ask is because of the qualification that in paragraph that you say the Serbs gave permission for one newspaper, so I'm just trying to discover if there was more that one Albanian newspaper functioning at that time.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question with full certainty. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 4 of the English version of your statement, you discuss hearing things and you say that, Up until the time the newspapers were closed down, we reported to them what was happening. It's at the very bottom of the English, I believe. The very last line of the English on 4, so it may be 4 or 5. The paragraph starts in English with: "The Serbs had large cannons placed..." So it may be actually on the next page in the Albanian. And the line in English reads: "Up until the time that the newspapers were closed down, we reported to them what was happening." What time-period are you talking about here?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the time-period March/April 1998, up until the 23rd of March when the police searched and broke into the premises of our council.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So how many newspapers were you reporting to that were operational up until the 23rd of March?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember "Koha Ditore" and "Bujku" as two of these newspapers. "Koha Ditore" was being published before the war. I remember it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. So how many newspapers were shut down in 1998 and 1999 if those two were operational?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number of daily newspapers published at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Back on the previous page you are talking about firings that go on. Actually, I believe it's on page 2 back at the beginning, the first page of the statement. Somewhere in the middle of the page you say the Serbs suffered no problems. And this is in regard to the 1400 people living in the Gjakova municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in regard to the Serb citizens who lived in Gjakove municipality. They didn't have any problems whatsoever with employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But as we discussed prior, it was approximately 1500 people in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You also state that few Albanians could accept conditions imposed by the Serbs. What were these conditions?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about employment?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: It's in the same paragraph. And you are discussing people being fired, and you say: "The only way to retain your job was to except," but I think you mean accept "the conditions imposed by Serbia. Few Albanians could do this and suffered the consequences." I'm wondering what those conditions are.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please give me the reference?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: It's page 2 of the English, it's on your screen in front of you, I believe. The paragraph starts with: "During this period in Gjakove, people have been ..." Probably about two-thirds of the way down. The last paragraph maybe. It's on the first page of the statement for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may assist, I believe this is paragraph 4 of page 1 of the Albanian version, it's been formatted differently in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The one starting "Since 1988 ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: The paragraphs are lined up different apparently on this, so my paragraph starts at a different part. But basically I'm looking at the sentence that says specifically: "The only way to retain your job was to except the positions ..."

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If one wanted to retain his or her job, they had to sign a declaration of loyalty to accept the Serbian conditions and curriculum, to be ready to work under Serb orders. The majority of Albanians did not accept this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was this all positions or certain positions that were asked to sign this declaration of loyalty?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the Albanians were imposed this declaration of loyalty. The Serbs continued their employment normally. The only way to retain your job was to accept these imposed conditions.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What I was asking, actually, was did it apply to all professional fields, or were there only specific professional fields that were asked to sign this?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applied to all professional fields.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to sign one in your position?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Actually, not in all professional fields, mainly in administration and high-ranking positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this was just government positions; correct? State positions?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did any Albanians sign this statement of loyalty?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a group of Albanians, policemen, loyal to the Serb state collaborators.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Are you saying that only police signed this?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this group of Albanian policemen as the category of loyal citizens to the Serb government. They were all from villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What ramifications did they have for signing this, if any?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who were these who signed these agreements? None of the Albanians did.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you just stated some Albanian policemen had signed the statement of loyalty; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. But what kind of consequences are we talking about? The consequences that these policemen suffered?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm asking in general, but if you know of anything related to these police?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a consequence, they were ignored by the majority of the Albanians. They were an artificial creation so to say, and they were a minority. They gained power as policemen who were loyal to the authorities. They were looked down upon by the majority of the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you are referring to these people at page 3 of the statement, see if I can find where it is here exactly, you are saying that these people -- it's paragraph 2 in the English, so it may be further down on the page. It starts off -- at least the English paragraph says that: "These people that the Serbs found were not the intellectuals, they used people as I've described..." So are you stating that there were no Albanian intellectuals working in Gjakova municipality in the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the key positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You say that there were approximately 50 to 53 - not sure I have a reference on this - but 50 to 53 people out of the Albanian population who collaborated with the Serbs. Is that an estimate that you find fair?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the rumours in the town at the time. People had knowledge of this group of 50 or a little bit more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: In your testimony in Milutinovic et al., you were asked about human rights abuses, and you testified that you haven't had any case registered in which an Albanian has killed an Albanian. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the data I personally collected, cases that were reported to the office of the Council for the Defence of Human Rights and Freedom. I personally didn't have any such case registered in which an Albanian had killed another Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Despite the cases registered which you said were 1.000; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of persons killed?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: No, no, you took 1.000 cases registered?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Despite those, have you heard in general of any Albanians committing crimes against other Albanians during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that I took down only those cases that were reported to me by the victims. I cannot speak of other cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I was actually just referring to your personal knowledge, things you have heard around town, not necessarily something you took in a statement.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fighting was between the Serbs and the Albanians. Not between Albanians themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So I'll understand that answer to be a no. You know of no case where an Albanian has killed another Albanian in the conflict; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally I don't know of any such case.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And we have your interview from the OTP --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of one case that occurred after the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I think we are going to try to refrain to 1998 to 1999 in the period that we are discussing here today as far as things go. Thank you. But we have your interview here from 2001 from the OTP. What other interviews have you given to judicial organs?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judicial bodies, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you give any interviews to anyone else, a non-judicial organisation?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I've given interviews to the papers, to the media, but I don't believe I've spoken to any judicial bodies except for the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. In regard to these media interviews --

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we could have D004-2194 on the screen please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm going to refer to this "Los Angeles Times" article that you were asked about in your prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I believe if we go right away to -- it's -- we only have it in English, I'm afraid. If we go right away to what is e-court page 3 at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you remember giving this interview?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And at the bottom of this, and I'll just read it so you have the proper translation, it says: "The fate of those collaborators remains a mystery. Many, including the Jakupis, apparently decamped with the retreating Serbian forces. Others, Haxhibeqiri said, were caught by the Kosovo Liberation Army fighters and executed in apparent violation of Geneva Convention rules governing conduct during the war." And it's referring to collaborators here that you've discussed before. And I know that Milutinovic you said that those were not your words. Are those your words or not?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I have also said that I tried to put the record straight in the "Koha Ditore" newspaper the following day. And during the break, I can bring you that article of "Koha Ditore" where I put the record straight on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That was what I wanted to ask you.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was either a mistranslation or a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What did you mean to say in that paragraph or what did you say that you think was misunderstood?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please read it once again, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: "The fate of those collaborators remains a mystery. Many, including the Jakupis, apparently decamped with the retreating Serbian forces. Others, Haxhibeqiri said, were caught by KLA fighters and executed in apparent violation of the Geneva Conventions rules governing conduct during war."

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not said that bit about they being captured by the KLA and being executed by the KLA because I couldn't have said that. I didn't have any facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you are saying the journalist put this in himself?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may have been a misunderstanding. He maybe didn't understand me clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I know in your prior testimony you said that you did print this retraction --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or it may have been mistranslated by the translator because the conversation took place with the help of a translator.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That's completely understandable, which is why I was asking what you had said that could have been mistranslated, if you had any idea?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have been more accurate if I had the Albanian script in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you also read me the quotation which you did earlier?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If you don't remember, we can move on because you said you did print a retraction to this.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can bring a copy of the article in "Koha Ditore" where I put the record straight. And I have it with me; I can bring it after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That's excellent. Because you did say you weren't sure in your prior testimony where you printed a retraction, but you did say that it was the next day, you thought, because you were so upset about what this had said. You said also that you would give a copy to the OTP in this. Have you ever handed over a copy?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've brought it with me. I promised that I would bring a copy and I've done so. It was published in the world addition of "Koha Ditore" which is published in Switzerland. That was published on the 20th of January or February, I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Of the next year, the following year, because this article was in October of 1999, so it would have been January of the next year, 2000?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [English] January 20, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Is there a reason it didn't publish for three months? Is there a reason it took so long to publish the retraction?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, I wrote this article the next day after the original article was published. I read the "Los Angeles Times" article, then the following day I put the record straight with the "Koha Ditore" newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, you said in your prior testimony you would give a copy to the OTP, you would send a copy to them. Did you ever do that?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the last time I didn't have it with me, but I promised that I would bring it to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And that was in August of 2006; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you didn't bring a copy or give it to them even in speaking with them this week, you kept it in your own papers?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave them some photographs documenting the crimes, and they said that there are some which cannot be accepted as -- in evidence, but you can leave them for the archives. And this one I kept.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm merely just asking because in your transcript at 1193 of Milutinovic, you were asked: "Could you deliver a copy if necessary?" And you said: "I don't have a copy with me now, but I can send it to the Tribunal later." And it was never sent to the Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody asked for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But they did ask for it in that trial, did they not?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not -- no. No one.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: We can put the transcript on the screen, if it's helpful, which is 65 ter 5323, page 1193. And they say: "Could you deliver a copy ..." Did you not take that as them wanting a copy of this retraction?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May I ask, Ms. O'Leary, the matter on the screen, did you want to tender that?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That was his statement, Your Honour. I believe it was tendered yesterday as P1068. Oh, you are right, Your Honour, I'm sorry, we did move on to the "LA Times" article. I would seek to tender that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00306, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But to go to the question: Did you not consider "Can you deliver a copy ..." did you not consider that them wanting a copy? And specifically the words are: "Could you deliver a copy if necessary?"

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was my answer then?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Your answer was: "I don't have a copy with me now, but I can send it to the Tribunal later."

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as it happens, I'm here again.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But it's now three years later. Did you not find it important to that trial to send in the retraction?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was expecting someone to ask me for it. I was expecting someone to tell me, Can you send me that denial. And if that question was put to me, then I would have sent it to whoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You did find it important enough to bring with you this time, though; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say it was not important. I said that I was expecting the Tribunal to call me and say send me the denial. This is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You don't think, though, that you saying "I can send to the Tribunal later" was enough of an affirmation they would rely on when they said "Thank you." You thought you would be asked additionally?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm saying it that no one called me to say, Please send it to us. I didn't know how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haxhibeqiri.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now I want to talk about people leaving and some expulsions, quickly a few questions here. You stated yesterday that the Albanians in the neighbourhood that you were hiding in were ordered to leave and that was about 20.000 to 30.000 people were ordered to leave?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When was this specifically?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was exactly on the 2nd of April. On the 1st or the 2nd, but it's more on the 2nd.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How do you know these people were ordered to leave?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there when the police arrived and started evicting people from their homes, telling them to go. If you don't go, we will bomb your houses. So everyone was forced to leave their homes and take their journey towards Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But at that time you also had stated that you were in a pipe or a pothole in the backyard, so you didn't actually see these people leaving, did you?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw the people, I was not in the water-pipe hole, but I was looking at what was going on from behind the curtains. They gave an ultimatum to the people, You've got five minutes to leave your homes or else.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But subsequent to that, you didn't actually see people leaving, did you?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were all ready with their bags and luggage they could manage to get with them and they were ready to go. They were all the time under enormous pressure and under threats, and they were anxious to know what was going to happen with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: The reason I ask is because in your previous testimony at 1153, you did say: "On the 2nd of April when they had driven out almost 30.000 people from that neighbourhood, I remained in that pothole because I was afraid to come out and cross the border because I was an activist and I was afraid my name would be black-listed. This is the reason I remained there hidden." So it if you were in the pipe at that time --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I was frightened and terrified that they could get me.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If you were hiding in that pipe, you didn't actually see the people leaving, is what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that at the moment, at the time when the police forces arrived, I was in my house, and I was looking at what was going on from behind the curtains of my house. And I saw them as I left the house too. I saluted them. And after a time, I went into that water-pipe hole.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. I'm about to go into an area where we discussed the periods of time that you are hiding, so this may be an adequate time for the break if Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, we will have the first break now and resume at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While the witness is coming in, Ms. O'Leary, could we point out that you have been cross-examining on the Milutinovic transcript. It is not an exhibit, if you need to be aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We didn't make any plan to tender the whole thing because it is quite long, so I was just going to read the relevant passages if that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's fine. As long as you are aware.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. O'Leary.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And before we begin, just so everyone is aware, we are now accompanied by our legal intern, Mr. Eric Durand just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, I wanted to discuss these periods that you were in hiding, because during this very important period, there's a couple different times when you were sheltered or in different hiding places, and it was discussed yesterday to some degree. And the first time you went into hiding is on the 23rd of March; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 23rd of March, I left my home from the Hadum neighbourhood and I went to the Blloku i Ri neighbourhood. I went into hiding on the 2nd when police forces arrived and they evicted the population from their homes in that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But from the 23rd to the 31st, 1st, 2nd, for that week in there, ten days, where were you?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Blloku i Ri neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this was at your relatives house, the doctor, with the others, 15, 16 people?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There were eight of us in that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Eight of you. From the 23rd until the 2nd you were there? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that neighbourhood, yes. I remember one or two days I stayed in the house of a friend of mine during that period. The 23rd and the 24th I stayed in the house of a friend of mine which was near the house of the doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you were in the Blloku i Ri neighbourhood starting from the 23rd, at your friend's, from the 23rd to 24th; and then from the 25th to the 2nd you were exclusively at?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you ever leave the doctor's house between the 25th and the 2nd?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I stayed in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Because I don't know if you recall, but you had said in Milutinovic that you were there a week, which actually from the 23rd to the 2nd would be a bit more than a week, more like a week and a half?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The figures have always been approximate.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. But from the doctor's house that's where you say you saw houses burning on the 26th of March, from the 2nd floor of the house, you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: 27th.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I saw things also on the 26th. Also on the night of the 25th. I saw houses being burned almost every night.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you say "every night," for what period of time? How long, when did it start, when did it end?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about these dates, the 25th, the 26th, and the 27th. During all the time that I stayed in the doctor's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And those houses burning yesterday you said were about 60 to 100 to 200 metres away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so I'm assuming some were burning closer at about 60 [Realtime transcript read in error "600"] metres but then some were further on about 200 metres away?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they could be seen from where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this was six houses you saw burning on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were also on one occasion ten houses burning, but I cannot remember exactly when -- which was when. There were two houses on one occasion, ten houses on another.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That's understandable. I was taking the six from your statement, actually, you had said at page six that you saw six houses on the 26th, so I was just confirming. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I interrupt to point out that page 32, line 6, in our transcript, you are quoted as having put in your question 600 metres, I believe your question was six zero, 60 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So how did you know that the houses that were -- especially the houses that were 200 metres away, how did you know that they were Albanian houses?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that area, I'm not aware of any Serb houses. Behind the house of the doctor, there is a big building which was inhabited by the Serbs and further on it was the headquarters of the Secretariat for Internal Affairs. Another building which was built by the Albanians but it was taken over by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But 200 metres is a pretty good distance away to know exactly which house is burning; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But when the fires were extinguished after a while, I identified all the houses that were burned down and I've got the names of the families to which they belonged, the names of the owners. You can see the flames, fires burning, even at a distance of 2.000 metres during the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you didn't see any of them being lit, correct, you only saw them when they were actually in flames?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I only saw it when they were burning. I have seen many cases, many occasions, when the houses were lit. When they were set alight. And it was -- the Romas were being used to set the houses of the Albanians alight.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How were the Romas being used?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking how they were setting the houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: No, I'm actually referring to what you just said, I was unclear as to when you said: "When they were set alight. And it was the Romas being used to set the houses the Albanians alight." I'm not sure what you mean, how were they using the Romas?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Serbian police who was using them. They were serving the policies of the Serbian state.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you say "they were using them," are you saying that Romas were lighting house on fire for the Serbian police, is that what I'm to take from that?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Romas have been seen while setting houses on fire. And I've also seen policemen who were setting houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you personally saw Romas and policemen setting the houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I saw only policemen. But there are other eye-witnesses in the town of Gjakove who've seen Roma set houses alight and looting houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: In your statement you said: "I did not see them set alight. I just saw them burning." When did you see the houses being set alight?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to my neighbourhood, the Hadum neighbourhood, there I saw them setting houses and shops alight.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll come back to that then, and we'll go back to the period of the 23rd to the 2nd where you are at the doctor's house. And on the 2nd you said you were in a house where two police showed up. This was the doctor's house; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And who was in the house with you then?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The eight of us that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: The people who you are referring to as police, who did they speak to?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the owner of the house, the lady.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was everyone else hiding or did they speak to anybody else?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the others were not hiding. I was the only one hiding at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you were hiding because you thought because of your activist position that the police were looking for you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you said: "I was hiding in the house but I saw and heard them." Where exactly were you hiding in the house?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw them, I was not hiding at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So when the police --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me this question for the fifth time, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I apologise, I'm just a little unclear as to where you were in the house.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you have problems understanding me or linguistic problems. What do you want to know?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I want to know what happened on the 2nd of April. I want to know the sequence of events that happened when the police came and where you were.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer your question. On the 2nd of April, about 25.000 people were expelled from that area and were directed in the direction of Albania. So all the residents of that area left.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But there were eight people in the house that you were in including yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And when the police showed up at the door, all eight, including yourself, were there; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And so you weren't hiding at that time when the police showed up?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you had an unobstructed view of the people who you refer to as "police"; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And how do you know that they were police?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you said in your prior testimony yesterday that one was wearing a light blue uniform and one was wearing a regular blue uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was wearing a blue uniform and the other was wearing an olive colour uniform. Military colour uniform. This was one of those loyal policemen that I mentioned who belonged to that small minority of 50 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: The one in the olive uniform or the one in the light blue uniform was a part of those 50 people?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one with the olive uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And he was an Albanian; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I think you referred to him as Mushk Jakupi's son; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of that organisation headed by Mushk Jakupi or Musa Ibraj, what is his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How did you know that he was police if he was wearing an olive uniform, is that a colour you typically associate with the police in Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were people who had been recruited as policemen. From 1993 onwards, the Albanian policemen had been expelled from the state organs. This group, in order to give the impression that there are still Albanians within the ranks of the police, were recruited by the authorities, and, as I said, they were referred to as artificial creations, as bastards, who did not enjoy the support of the majority of the Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And were serving the then Serbian regime.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So if you are saying that this group of people was enlisted to give the impression that there were still Albanians within the ranks of police, are you saying they had no real power?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have much power, I would say. However, there are situations in which they proved themselves loyal to the authorities, and they did have the power to kill, to beat up, and persecute people.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So the man wearing an olive drab uniform is Albanian of this artificial creation you say, and the other person is wearing what?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it light blue or dark blue?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Light blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it a uniform you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had seen such uniform on a daily basis. It was a police uniform. He was wearing that type of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you know what that person's ethnicity was, is?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How do you know he was a Serb?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that later on by people who recognised him.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you were told that, did someone tell you his name?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember it?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Domitca [phoen] Avramovic he worked in the Secretariat of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So when they came around and they told the people there in the house to leave and to go to Albania, it was actually one Albanian and one Serb who were doing the expulsion at that time?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And at least one of them didn't have very much power as an artificial creation, as you said?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Less. Less than the other. He was a tool. I think he was given that task because of the language.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And following that, the police left, and you said that you saluted them just earlier?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police continued to go to every house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But they left. Right before the break you said you saluted them and they went on their way; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I went back to my hiding place.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You hadn't been in the pipe before that, had you?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had been in the pipe hole before. I had prepared a strategy in order to rest a little bit. The eight of us would go to that water-pipe hole which was 1.2 by 1.4 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: At what point before April 2nd were you in that hole?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th when it suited me to use that hole as a shelter, as a hiding place. The other seven people who were with me liked the idea, and on the 27th when the houses were being burned and people were being killed, we decided to take shelter, all of us, in that water-hole -- water-pipe hole.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So it was sporadically over the course of March 24th, 5th, well after the 27th to the 2nd that you would use that hole when you were afraid that somebody --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all times. Only when the police units would come in that area. Because of fear, we would take shelter into that hole thinking that that might be the way for us to survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But if you are hiding in this hole and you are afraid of the police, why were you not afraid of the two police that came to the door and spoke to the eight of you on the 2nd of April?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak to the policemen. As I said, it was the landlady who spoke with them. I was behind the door, behind the curtain and from there I could hear the conversation, what she was being told by them. I didn't go outside in the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I apologise. I misunderstood then where your positioning was. So you didn't actually face-to-face see the policemen who came to the yard that day, or who you say are policemen, you saw them through the curtain; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. You got it right.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And from what distance were you?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15 metres. About 15 metres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was anyone with the landlady when she spoke to them?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them, I would say, were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Everyone except you; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you. And so in your statement when you say you go into the pipe in the backyard on the 2nd then, I'm assuming this is after the police leave you decided to head to that pipe and hide out there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you were there -- hid in the water-pump hole for four days and night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So we are at April 6th now, does that sound about right?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 5th.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. And so on the 5th and after you come out of the water-pipe your statement says: "After four days I returned to my own house and stayed until the war was over." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why was it safe to return to your house after the 5th? Had something changed, or why did you feel it was okay to go home at that point?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the risk.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And in your statement you say: "I knew they were looking for me," this is all on page 7 of the English, "I knew they were looking for me, I had spoken to my colleagues from my office who had been released and they told me the police wanted me." Correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Why did the police not come looking for you at your house?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only myself, but all the activists of the council were being sought by the police. They were looking for me on the 1st and the 2nd day.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then they stopped looking for you, after the 1st and 2nd day?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They called me on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What day did they call you on the phone?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days after the bombing started, on the 25th or the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I am assuming you didn't have a mobile phone at that time?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. It was a land-line.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So they would have called you at what residence?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't call me directly, but a friend of a niece of mine was contacted via phone by them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And what did they say to her?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this Fuat's house? And she said, no, it isn't. And then they said, Sorry, then I guess we called the wrong number. Do you know Fuat's number? But at that time there was nobody in my house because my uncle's house, which is in the same courtyard with my own house, was burned. They thought that it was my house actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: At that time you were in the Blloku i Ri neighbourhood; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And who was on the phone? Did they identify themselves in any way? Who called your niece's friend?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said they were police.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you speak directly with the friend or with your niece who heard from the friend?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My niece told me about this and then I wanted to speak with her friend in person about this. And my niece told me that I should run away because I was being searched by them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Were you aware that you hadn't mentioned this phone call in your statement before or in previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I failed to mention many, many things because I wasn't asked about everything. I have many things to say, and a statement is too small for everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you used that as the basis of how you knew the police were looking for you; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So it's fairly important to why you were hiding; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It was a sign. Not only the phone call, but the fact that the personnel of the council was arrested on the 23rd and the 24th. And the fact that I was told by members of the personnel that I was being looked for is another reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you have no way of being certain who was actually on the phone with the niece's friend, do you?
