utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not important at the time. I only mentioned it as a detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So from the 5th of April you were at your house?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were being actually killed. Phone calls were of no importance at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: From the 5th of April you were at your house; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And that's through the remainder of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the exception of those ten days when I went to my uncle's house in another neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What ten days did you go to your uncle's house, approximately?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in April. Mid-April.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If I could have P1069 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That was the map that you marked yesterday so we can kind of see perhaps where you were for those ten days. In the time that you were at your house from the 5th until mid-April before you went to your uncle's house, did you go out at all, or did you stay only in your house?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went outside the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you speak with anybody?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You ran into people on the street?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mainly women and elderly, who were moving from one neighbourhood to another carrying food stuffs with them and going to bury their family members in house yards. They didn't dare bury their family members with a full ceremony in the city cemetery because of the police. More than 30 bodies were buried in house yards.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This too is not in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. You said there's a lot that's not in your statement. Where were the young men at that time if you say you only saw -- sorry, I didn't get the answer.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was important for the Tribunal. The youth were very careful. They tried to avoid the streets because of the kidnappings and killings. Had they been found on the streets, they would have been killed or kidnapped or arrested or tortured.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Is it possible that the young men were involved in the KLA and that's why you didn't see them on the streets?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little. Very few young men were in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you perceive the KLA to have a strong presence in Gjakova then?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you personally know anyone who was involved with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And I want to move on then to the damage to the cultural heritage that you've discussed in your statement here, and you say at page 3 in the English that from 1990 all the Albanian statues were destroyed by the Serbs. I want to focus on 1998 and 1999 and what was destroyed in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Gjakove and its outskirts, about 6.000 such buildings were damaged. Can you give me the reference, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Of course. It's on page 3 in the English. It is approximately midway through. And the English paragraph starts with: "I have been asked about any damage to cultural heritage." I'm guessing on the Albanian it might be towards the end of page 3 or the beginning of page 4 as these are lining up.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the page number.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: It seems we are having a little technical problem. Let me just ask you what you know about the mosques in Gjakova. We can specifically talk about that without your statement right now. How many mosques were there in Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eleven, to what I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And in 1998 and 1999 which ones suffered damage in the conflict? How many is fine.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main one, which is the biggest in Kosova. The one that was built 400 years ago. Actually, the anniversary was in 2004. But not only mosques but also old houses with architectural value like the house of Ali Aga and obelisk.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. I want to focus just on the mosques right now, and we can move on to other damage as we move on. But with the mosques, you say there were 11 in town and you focused on the damage to the main mosque that was 400 years old. Was there damage sustained to the other mosques in town?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, yesterday when we were talking about this main mosque you said you observed or witnessed the damage and I believe you stated: "Yes, on the 7th or 8th, I'm not sure, I was in the courtyard of my house when the minaret of the mosques, from what I believe to be an internal explosion, collapsed." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whether it was internal or external explosion, that I don't know for sure, but I know that there was this cloud of smoke when the minaret collapsed. I only saw the minaret as it collapsed.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes, I believe in your prior testimony you were asked specifically: "Can we conclude you did not see this directly?" And your answer was: "Yes, the debris fell on my book, yes, and I heard the explosion and later I saw that the minaret was cut in half." Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is accurate. I saw it directly. I had my book in my hands, and I just looked up and saw the minaret collapse. And the debris fell on my head as I was with my book in my hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So the thing I'm confused about is did you actually see it collapse, or did you hear the explosion and look up and it was in two? Which was it?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the minaret collapse. After the debris fell.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So it's not accurate to say that the debris fell on my book, I heard the explosion, and later I saw the minaret was cut in half. That's not accurate. You actually saw it?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it as it was coming down.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So your testimony in the prior trial was not accurate regarding that? What did I say in the previous trial?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: For reference of the parties, it's at T1201, lines 3 through 9, in Milutinovic. You said -- the question asked to you was: "So we can conclude that you did not see this directly. That you only heard the explosion and then saw the fragments that flew into your room; is that right?" And your answer was: "Yes, the debris fell on my book, yes, and I heard the explosion. And later I saw the minaret was cut in half."

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the dust and the debris that was caused by the explosion, when the view in front of me was clear, then I saw that it had collapsed.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And where --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the scale of damage then.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. So once the clouds passed, the debris, you saw it was in two?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Where were you at that time when the clouds passed and you saw the minaret in two?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the courtyard of my own house and I was facing the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm a little confused then because yesterday when you said that you were in the courtyard of your house, you followed that with: "At that moment I went up on the second floor and from the roof I was following the developments, and within five minute, the minaret collapsed and I saw no one there." So when did you go up to the roof-top of your house?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When did you go up to the roof-top?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after the explosion I ran upstairs to observe the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So just so that I'm clear on this, you were in the backyard reading a book, you heard an explosion, there was debris, you looked up, you saw the minaret was in two, and then you went up to your roof to follow developments; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: That is, thank you very much. And at that time you --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At last.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thanks for bearing with. And you said at that time: "I saw no one there." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you have no information as to how the damage was caused, personally?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that NATO didn't bomb it.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you to eliminate possibilities. I was just saying you simply had -- have no direct knowledge of how it collapsed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And as a related matter, when we were just discussing, you were outside in your yard on the 8th of May, and I believe you said in your previous testimony it was 13.08 in the afternoon, that's correct, about the time?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 7th, that's the accurate date. On the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Approximately 1.00 p.m.; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was exactly 1.07.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you have a walled courtyard at your house?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The courtyard in the direction of the mosque, it was surrounded by shops which were all burned down and I could see them from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm not asking directly about your view right now. I'm just wondering if you had walls on the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of the mosque, the courtyard bordered shops which were burned down.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's to say that I had a clear view from the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You've stated in both your previous testimony and in your statement that the 7th to the 11th of May was the worst infighting between the KLA and the VJ in Gjakova; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And it's at that point that the minaret collapsed in some fashion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What moment are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I'm talking about the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 7th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you were outside in the afternoon reading a book, it was safe enough to do that?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you weren't obliged to leave as others had been directed to do?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat your question once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I was asking since it was May 7th and you were still there in your courtyard, you weren't obliged to leave as you had said many of the Albanian citizens had been directed to do?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not communicate with them. I was in my own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I guess maybe if I rephrase it. Why did you stay in Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why are you asking that?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Because if the majority of the population is being forced to leave by the police and the military as you are saying, and the police are looking for you, as you are saying, I'm wondering why you were not obligated to leave as an Albanian citizen?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that I was not obligated to leave, but I said that I feared that I would be caught by the police and during all the time I was very careful not to be visible in my movements.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did the police stop looking for you at that time, by the 7th of May?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The question seems irrelevant. I don't know what you are asking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking because at that time you felt it safe enough to be open in your yard and to walk on the streets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was monitoring the movement of the forces, and I knew the time when they were moving around, and there was a time that I felt a little bit safer. When the fighting paused, it was a bit calmer. And during that time I availed myself of the opportunity to do something, to read, and I was probably trying to divert my mind from what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But you stated three times now then that the 7th to the 11th was the worst fighting, infighting between the KLA and the VJ in Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you consider the possibility that the police were not actually looking for you?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, I want to return to the house burnings that we discussed before and I said I would come back to, because you said from your house you saw a couple of fires each day. You said earlier today that you personally saw houses being alit?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And in your statement I believe you say: "I saw paramilitaries set those houses on fire. They would throw small plastic containers with petrol and then shoot them at the houses on fire." Did you actually see that happening with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it with my own eyes. And then they shot these containers and the shop was set alight. I've seen shops being burned that way. Whereas the office of the Council For the Human Rights and Freedoms was burned, and I've seen that, by using a match. They set the curtains alight and then the flames took the whole place. Within three to four hours, all the evidence that we had collected for this Tribunal was burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During these four days. Sometime around the 5th or the 6th. Sorry, the 8th, the 9th, but that was during this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Of which month?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, you've mentioned in your statements before -- sorry, there was no interpretation; you didn't say the month.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was between the 7th and the 11th of May, talking about this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you are saying you actually saw someone light a match to the curtains in your office and set it on fire in that time?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it myself together with my brother. From the roof of our house which was partly burned and with no tiles on. Part of the roof was uncovered, talking about the roof of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How far away were you -- I apologise. How far away were you to see that?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 100, 130 metres. Probably closer. 120.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you couldn't actually see who was lighting it, but you say you saw someone with a match at 120 metres away lighting the curtains?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about 50 police and paramilitary forces with armbands and bandanas. They entered every shop and business and office, and I've seen a large number of shops being burned. And there were 20 shops in a row which were burned by these forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And if it's the 7th to the 11th of May and there's infighting between the VJ and the KLA as you've testified to, then the KLA was present there too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the Qabrati Hill, in the suburbs of the town, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But are you telling me in your testimony today that you could identify the person 120 metres away who had a match in his hand lighting the curtains of your office? You could identify what forces he was with?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, judging by the uniforms that they were wearing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What was he wearing that you could tell from 120 metres?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the paramilitary forces were --

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to describe what they were wearing. They were wearing -- they were in camouflage uniforms, and you could see the armbands which were not of the police or the regular army. They were paramilitaries who were working hand-in-hand with the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: We'll get to that in a few moments. But you are telling me you could see the armbands from 120 metres away?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I could identify them because I've seen them from close up too; five metres away. I could see them as they were going past my house every day; I've seen police and paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Was it night-time?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Can you describe the armband that you saw?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the guy who set the offices alight, but I have noticed that armband in hundreds of paramilitary forces like that. As people may see me wearing this headset, I could see the armbands on these people just like that. From a close distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, I'm actually putting to you that 120 metres is a pretty long distance to notice an insignia or an armband. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then it could have been a shorter distance. But I couldn't be so accurate, as it were. And maybe it was 80 metres. And I could see them carrying towels because it was very hot because of the burning of the houses and shops. Actually, they were in one of the businesses playing pool, and then they came out and they set the businesses and shops alight. Ten or 15 of them in that row.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How do you know they were playing pool?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see them from my house. Opposite my house there was a business where you could play pool, and from atop my house you could see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you are saying you could see in, you saw these gentlemen playing pool, you saw them come out, go 100 metres away, strike a match, and light buildings including your office; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't go further away. They were in the shops and they set those shops alight. I was about 100 metres away and saw what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I know that in your statement, and I believe your prior testimony, you've mentioned that your Agimi firm - I'm going to mispronounce it - I know you've mentioned that that was burned on the 24th; but this is the first I believe you've said that your council's office was burned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Agimi that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You've mentioned that prior, but you've not mentioned that your council office was burned.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have mentioned that in my statement. And you find that on the transcript as well. I remember very well three years ago I've said the same. Just like I'm saying it now. Because it's very clear in my mind's eye, and I was crying when I saw the offices where I worked were in flames. And I will never forget that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, your transcript is quite long, I would have to review it again to ensure, but it's not contained in your statement, I don't believe. And it should be pretty fundamental, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can read that on the transcript, if you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. O'Leary, is this a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, would the Chamber be correct in anticipating you will finish today?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's quite brief after this. We are wrapping up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Unfortunately, I am not able to be present for the last sitting; I must be elsewhere in the building. The other two judges will continue the hearing under Rule 15 bis. We will adjourn now and resume at 6.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUGGE
utterances.text: Ms. O'Leary, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you'll be happy to know we're going to try to finish this up very briefly here, but I have a few more things I want to clarify. Over the break, I had an opportunity to look through your statement again and through all of your testimony, and to be honest I did not see that you mentioned that your council's office was burned. I did see that the Agimi firm was burned, but I did not see anything about the council's office being burned. In particular I'm concerned about that not being in your statement, because in 2001 you were the chairman; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And this statement, after it was taken, was read back to you in a language that you understood; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you signed this statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you signed it without asking them to include in there that your council's office was burned?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there were other even more interesting things that were left out, things that have more weight. As I said, the statement is incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: But as the chairman, wouldn't that be fairly important to you?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement is incomplete. However, during my testimony here three years ago, I'm sure I mentioned that, the burning of the council's office. Something that I saw myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, is this on Asim Vokshi Street? Is this where the council's office was?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Because on page 8 of your statement in English you do discuss --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's one street below Asim Vokshi Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And you did discuss that there was definitely burning.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the street is Ilir [phoen] Vula.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You discuss that there was burning, but you did not discuss your own council's office. Wouldn't that have been sufficiently important to include in your statement to the Tribunal as the chairman?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it was an omission on my part. Do you think it was a mistake that I did not include that in my statement? I think that if I failed to mention it then, I'm mentioning it now and the honourable Judges can hear about it now. However, I will underline it again that I did mention the fact that the council's office was burned during my previous testimony three years ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And to be fair, I'm not actually questioning that your office was burned, I'm questioning that you actually saw it from 120 metres, that somebody who you describe as paramilitary took a match and lit it, inside the building? Did you personally eye-witness this?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I eye-witnessed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Let's move on then. I have a map up on the screen, it's the one you marked yesterday. And I think I want to have you mark on here a couple of things and hopefully in a different colour than red so that we know the difference. But if you could mark on there, do you know where the Catholic church of St. James was?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no church of St. James in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Are there any Catholic churches in Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: What are they named?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is the St. Paul Catholic church in Gjakove. We are talking about the town; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Yes. Where is the Catholic church of St. James then? Is it in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of a church by the name of St. James in Gjakove municipality. There are two churches in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you were asked in your testimony prior, you were asked: "Why is the damage to the Catholic church of St. James in Djakovica not mentioned here?" And you answered - not that it didn't exist - you answered: "The church did not function. There was collateral damage done to it by the NATO air-strikes. That was an old church. That church did not have permission to be built in the first place, and after the war they built a new church which was the highest building in Gjakova. During the war it was also mined by the Serbian forces and NATO came later and demined the church, although it wasn't functioning as a church at all. It was damaged, yes. It was not me who organised this exhibition." And here you are discussing a book. And then you were asked - after discussing a book: "But can we agree it was damaged by NATO bombing?" And you say: "Yes." So I am wondering where this St. James church is?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the mosque of St. Dao [phoen], a Franciscan which was opposite the VJ army barracks at the time. Because of the bombing of the army barracks, the new church, although it was next to the army barracks, did not suffer major damages, only some collateral damages. The NATO air-strikes were very precise when hitting their targets. They did not bomb civilian facilities. They only bombed military and police facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Do you know then -- well, let me follow up on that, so you were mistaken about what you were being asked and you thought you were being asked about a mosque and not a Catholic church; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a church; it's not a mosque. The mosque is Muslim facility, whereas the church is a Christian one.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. Can you mark on this map where the Novi Blok neighbourhood is?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this part here.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Isn't it true that many homes were destroyed from a bomb there and caught fire?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. Not a single bomb fell in Blloku i Ri with the exception of the bomb that hit the building of the SUP. On the 21st or the 22nd of May at around 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Is that location on this map where that bomb fell?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the legend on this map, so I can only assume. I can only point out the direction; it's the south-east.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we tender this marked map, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And then if we could have -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That, Your Honour, will be assigned D00307.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And if we could have P696 on the screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Isn't it true that NATO heavily bombed the Gjakova city and municipality during the air-strike campaign?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town of Gjakova, only the military and police facilities were bombed by the NATO forces. And only one civilian was killed. The first building that was bombed was the SUP building and this civilian who suffered from this bombing lived next to the SUP building. He happened to be in the bathroom when the SUP building was hit, and he was killed as the result of the bombing.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Are you aware of a bombing of a column of refugees in the Djakovica municipality just south of the city?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: How can you still categorise the NATO bombing as having precise targets? How do you explain that incident?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the town of Gjakove. The column was -- that was hit was outside the town. It was in a village.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So the NATO bombing campaign was only precise within the town of Gjakova is what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military and police targets or bases. With the exception of that civilian victim, the factory in the north part of the town was also targeted, although it was a civilian facility, but there was a large concentration of Serb police and military forces in the courtyard of the factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So what was the military or police target of the refugee convoy in May?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we should ask NATO about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the document on the screen. And if we go to page 2, I am afraid, again, I don't have this in Albanian. I can read out the relevant portion. We have it in English and in Serbian is the original on this. It is a Ministry of the Interior report and summary of events from 28 March, 1999. And if we're going a little bit -- I know you read some English or Serbian perhaps, maybe you can follow along if we are down. The very first paragraph discusses NATO attacks in Djakovica and it says: "In an attack by NATO armed forces on the Devet Jugovica barracks in Djakovica at around 2110 hours on 26 March 1999, the ammunition and military equipment depot was hit. The explosion caused a fire in which the facility burned down. Enormous material damage was caused to nearby houses, owned mainly by Serbs and Montenegrins." Is this the event you're speaking about in the northern part of the town?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe you are mistaken there, there is no Devet Jugovica barracks in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Okay. If we go further down in the paragraph, let's discuss where it says: "NATO planes also bombed the Novi Blok neighbourhood destroying around 40 family houses, which caught fire. Mark Malota, Morina, Hajdar Vula," it gives some dates, "and Mahkmut Vula all from Djakovica were killed. It is possible that more people were killed in this attack are buried under the ruins." Is that the area that I just had you mark on the map?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Are you saying that this document is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely incorrect. There is no grain of truth in it. I've spoken to the parents of those killed from the Vula family, with Mark Malota, I spoke one or two days before the event; or to be more precise, I was with him on the 23rd. He was arrested by the police and he was killed by the police. On the 26th, a bridge was -- he was thrown from a bridge. He was the leader of the LDK branch in Gjakova. As far as the other victims are concerned, they were in the Blloku i Ri neighbourhood. I was sheltering, and I could see the police forces at 4.00 in the morning escorted by about 20 jeeps and Pinzgauers with the headlights on only on the first vehicle. Those who watched the horror movies of Hitchcock can understand this situation, and the Hitchcock movies would be quite entertaining compared to the horror existing at the time. I'm explaining here how I felt at the time. I and other Albanians were persons on the Schindler's List, if you remember the movie.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, but we are running out of time. And I understand you have a lot to tell, but I do want to ask you, can you conceive it as possible that there were fires as a result and collateral effect from NATO bombing in Djakovica municipality and specifically the town?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no facts supporting that claim, that bombs fell in the town and hit civilian facilities, with the exceptions of the places that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I want to very briefly discuss, you speak about some murders and you list some victims in your statement, and in these you talk about what other people had told you. Now, isn't it true that you have never actually, in this time-period, you didn't witness anyone being murdered, you only heard about it or saw a body?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw killed persons myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did you see them actually being killed, or did you see them after they were already dead?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when they were already dead on the streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: So you don't know the exact cause of death of any of the people that you saw; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sufficient to be an Albanian to be killed by these forces which had no moral or legal responsibility. It was sufficient to be an Albanian. They had no humanitarian values either. They didn't feel sorry or responsible towards other human beings.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we go through your listing of what you have here, you discuss several incidents. The first ones were on page 7, the 25th of March, the 26th, the 27th, the 31st; we go on to the next page, the 1st, the 2nd, the 2nd, and the 4th. And at all of those times, you were in hiding, were you not?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When during that period were you not in hiding?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sheltering. I didn't fall into the hands of the police. I don't know what you mean by hiding. To take shelter means to avoid falling into the hands of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I think I was using the word hiding from your statement, and it may be -- you do use sheltering at one point on the 2nd. But when you are in the pipe, you do say, I hid in the water-pump hole.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, going into the water-pump hole, that is hiding. But the rest of the story is that I was avoiding being captured by the police, the paramilitary, or the army. I was vigilant all the time. I didn't sleep. I slept very little during those seven or eight days of terror.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, it also says hiding for the 26th on page 6 too. Were you hiding on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of which month?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: March.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, we entered the water-pipe hole when the forces entered the neighbourhood. We stayed there for a certain number of hours, one, two, and then we emerged from there, when we noticed that we were not in the immediate danger of being captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Well, I put to you then with these individual victims, that during this time you have witnesses that say that all of this was taken from statements and you did not eye-witness any of these events that follow "I have witnesses that say ..."?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specify please which events you are talking about? You cannot put everything under one sentence. Mention the dates, and I will answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If we can go -- if you are on page 6 in the English version, and in your statement it's probably 6 or 7. The reason I wasn't going one by one is because there are one, two, three, four, at least 15 different things that you talk about that you say other witnesses tell you. And so I'm asking you: Are these stories relayed from your information that you took from the council and you're just recalling from memory?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which dates are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: If you look at your statement where you say: "From my investigation I have witnesses that say ..." And the first one is Mark Malota. And somebody told you this story that you have here?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife -- sorry, Malota's wife told me the story.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Did we see Mark Malota's name in that last document, though, as being killed by a NATO bomb?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that Mark Malota was one of the leaders of the LDK party in Gjakove. He was the first activist of the party in town. He was arrested when he was distributing aid to the population, and he was arrested in the courtyard of the Mother Teresa Association.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You don't know this from personal knowledge though; correct? You know this from witnesses?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was reported to our office, this incident, and that was done via the telephone. And after the war, I spoke to his wife and also with the person who saw this happen with his own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he recognised Mark Malota.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, when you discuss these incidents, you say there's common evidence of police and paramilitary. But for each incident that you're listing, you don't know the specific perpetrators that were there. You've given no information here. And I want to know, were you recollecting this from memory when you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, I said I spoke to his wife and with the two others who were detained in the same place, one was released immediately after the incident, another one by the name of Gzim Puska [phoen], he was held for the duration of the night, and he was tortured, and he was released in the early hours of the morning, and he was -- he managed to escape alive. And he told me how Mark was still being held, and he was being tortured the following day --

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you are recollecting all of this --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me finish. Let me finish. The following day, the witness said, I saw him in front of the gate of my house. He was dead and there was blood on his head. Blood-stains on his head. And when I spoke to his wife, she said when we -- when we buried him, there were no signs of bullets penetrating his body.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: You are recollecting all of this from memory; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you want me to say these things differently? You asked me about the source of the information, I'm telling you, it was his wife who told me. What else do you want? Invite his wife here, and she will tell you about the body of her husband. Or I can bring the file which is about his case that we have. Before -- the last time I came here, I brought the file because there was confusion created between another leader who had a bullet on his head. And there was confusion about that, and I apologized for that confusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I am afraid we don't have that file here. That's why I was asking. I want know what your personal knowledge is and what you are recollecting.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have it on the transcript specifically. We spend half a day to explain and clarify this case. Alongside the other person that was killed from the Patzi [phoen] village who also died because of the tortures he went through, he was submitted to. Amidzic Alija [phoen], his name. He died on the 16th of January because of the tortures inside the building of the Secretariat for Internal Affairs. And about this case, I spoke to his wife. She came to my office, and I spoke to her. And the following day, I also went to their house and I recorded every detail of this case. And I took part in the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, I think we can short-circuit this a little bit. When you were here prior and you brought the case file, did you leave that with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that most of your information has come from the 1.000 witness statements that you've read?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When -- about the cases that you posed questions about, that was my information, personal information. And the rest which relates to the previous statement, I'm trying to bring to you all the details that I remember, and I'm trying to be responsible and truthful about all the things that I say.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: I appreciate that. We simply don't have the time to, in court, go through what details you have on each one of these, which is why I'm trying to figure out in whole what -- when I say witnesses, you are talking about taking statements; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you ask that question once again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it's not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: Of course. When you refer to witnesses that say those words in your statement, does that mean it's something that was told to you in the course of your taking statements?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I quote witnesses about the cases, about the cases that I have information about; and I mention name, surname, and all the things that they said. And I say witnesses say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: When you gave this statement and you listed these things, these were things that you were relaying from memory; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And is it possible that the stories have integrated in your mind to some degree where you cannot be specific about certain details?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I've said is possible because I have been trying to select and organise stuff for a book. These events are not forgettable. They cannot be forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And in prior testimony you've quite openly admitted that in your opinion Serbs are the opponent side or that they are the belligerent force and in your frame of mind the Serbs are the enemy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I say Serbian politics, and at no time I have said the Serbian people because it wasn't the Serbian people, it was the Milosevic regime.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: And Your Honour -- I am sorry, please. I would have no further questions. I would like to put on the record, though, that the retraction that he said he was from the "Koha Ditore" that he mentioned that he could provide to the Chambers, if he could hand that over to the Prosecution or somebody so we could see this retraction that would be -- this is a specific request because last time it seemed a little vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. O'Leary. Ms. Kravetz, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have re-examination. I'll try my best to finish the next five minutes

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you were asked some questions earlier today about the burning of houses. And this is at page 34 or today's transcript. And you were asked whether you saw Roma police setting houses on fire. And you said you only saw police and you referred to having seen this when you went to your neighbourhood, the Hadum neighbourhood. I wanted to ask you specifically about what time-period you were referring to when you went to the Hadum neighbourhood, if this was in the period when you've spoken about that you returned after the 5th of April, or if this was another period you were referring to when you went to the neighbourhood and saw police setting fire to houses?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was for the whole period of 78 days. With the exception of the time when I was asleep but during -- or when I was in hiding, otherwise all the time I was monitoring the situation and I could see how the police forces were working hand in hand with the paramilitary forces and the army by burning the houses before looting them. I've seen columns of people leaving, being forced and threatened to leave. Threatened with weapons and being expelled to Albania. Being told, Go to Albania; this is Serbian land. Your country is Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you were also asked some questions about the burning of the offices of your organisation. When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 7th and the 11th of May. It was one afternoon. I cannot remember exactly whether it was the 9th or the 10th. It's most probably the 9th which is the middle part of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You also referred in one of your answers to my learned colleague about the burning of the offices of the organisation to seeing a group of about 50 police and paramilitaries, and you said, They entered every shop and businesses and office and I've seen a large number of shops being burned. When exactly did this happen that you saw this last large number of shops being burned?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That group, I did not see them only on the day when my office was burned. I saw that group every other day. They went into the people's houses, looted them, took their cars, and everything valuable inside these houses. They broke into these houses using sledgehammers and axes, and they threatened the population, pointing their weapons to their heads. And the honourable lady could say they are not included in the statement, but in my neighbourhood there were cases when immediately after the crime was perpetrated, I went to the place where it had happened and I saw with my own eyes in such a bad state. He was -- had been beaten up and tortured. And that happened from house to house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, we have very limited time.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [English] Okay, I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I'm just asking about this specific event that you spoke about, about seeing paramilitaries and police entering every shop and businesses and you said you saw a large number of shops being burned, when did that happen? Did that happen over a period of time? I'm just trying to understand when it happened?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one was on the 9th or the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where exactly did you see this large number of shops? I'm asking about which neighbourhood was it?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Hadum neighbourhood. At a distance of about 100 metres roughly from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in response to some questions by my learned colleague, you have said that in the period, I believe, from the 7th and the 10th of May there was intense fighting in Djakovica. Was there KLA presence in these shops you saw being burned, these businesses and shops?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were businesses and shops and homes of the Albanians. They were all civilians. The KLA was present in Qabrati Hill in the suburbs of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is part of the old Carshia of the old quarter of the town. It's a neighbourhood which is protected by the state.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, my final question relates to an answer you gave at page 39 of today's transcript. You were asked about the period between 27th and 2nd April and when you were hiding or whether you were hiding in that period in the water-pipe in the backyard of your relative's house. And you said you were not there all the time, only when police units would come in that area. Now, you've told us about the instance when the police came on 2nd of April. Were there other instances between the 27th of March and the 2nd of April when the police came to the area where you were hiding, to that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 27th and the 31st of March, I described one occasion when there were police forces arriving early morning. They burned a number of houses, and they killed eight people. In the meanwhile, on the 27th, they detained another 11 people from another family. That was in the Qerkezi [phoen] family. Six of them from one family, the Qerkezi family. The father and his four sons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you've given us two dates, the 27th of March and the 31st, and you've told us what happened on the 27th of March, what happened on the 31st?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 31st is another such date when six people were arrested. Just like on the 27th, the people who were arrested on the 27th and who were killed on the 27th, on the 31st, and later, their bodies were buried with no ceremony and they were exhumed a week later and they were sent in unknown direction. After the war, they identified more than 1.000 bodies or body remains which had been buried in the cemetery -- at a cemetery in Belgrade or that were found in the Danube, and in Batajnica. To this day, there are people who are missing. There were people who went missing in these dates. And the bodies have never been found.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions, and I apologise for going over time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Kravetz. This, Mr. Haxhibeqiri, is the end of your examination. The Chamber would like to thank you for the assistance you gave us to find out the truth. Thank you very much, again, and now you are free to return to your home. Thank you very much. And the Court Officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUGGE
utterances.text: And then we have to adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 9.00 in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of July, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
